chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The one performing Umra exclusively stipulates to his Lord that He releases him as He had withheld him, and the one performing the exclusive Hajj stipulates to his Lord: if it is not a Hajj, then (let it be) an Umra.

key_terms.عُمْرَةً مُفْرَدَةً: Exclusive Umrah (Umrah performed independently of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What are the correct stipulations for a pilgrim performing exclusive Umrah or exclusive Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific stipulations (shurut) pilgrims recite upon entering Ihram to manage potential impediments, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on proactive risk management in worship. It distinguishes between the Mufrad Umrah, which stipulates release from Ihram at the place of hindrance, and the Mufrad Hajj, which allows for conversion to Umrah if the Hajj is not completed, ensuring the validity of the ritual despite unforeseen circumstances.
